Definition: of uncertain derivation; Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of Europe:--Achaia.
BiblicalUsage: Achaia was the Roman province covering southern Greece, with Corinth as its capital, and Paul was hauled before Gallio its deputy, while its churches sent a gift to the poor saints in Jerusalem. As a place, Achaia is covered in the Biblical Places collection rather than in a biography.
TheologicalSignificance: Achaia is geography, not doctrine, and I will not dress it up as more. What matters is what happened there: ordinary believers in a Roman province gave generously to strangers, and Paul boasted of their readiness.
